title: A finite counterexample to the weighted Yamabe heat trace comparison
description: An explicit smooth weight on the round three-sphere exceeds the round Yamabe heat-trace maximum, with finite bounds and classical conformal geometry.
abstract: Morpurgo’s volume-normalized weighted Yamabe heat trace comparison, stated for every dimension at least three, is false in dimension three. We specify one smooth positive conformal weight on the round three-sphere whose scaled heat trace exceeds 13/20 at a specified positive time, whereas the round maximum is less than 321/500. The argument applies classical cylindrical conformal geometry and Dirichlet min–max estimates. A finite cylinder length, explicit smooth caps, and exact rational certificates give quantitative separation.
plain_language: A heat trace adds together the decaying contributions of all the vibration modes of an operator. The Yamabe operator combines the Laplacian with a curvature term. Multiplying its heat trace by a power of time lets us compare the largest value reached by different conformal weights while keeping the volume normalization fixed.

Morpurgo’s comparison asks whether the round sphere gives the largest such value for every smooth positive normalized weight, in every dimension at least three. This note gives a counterexample on the three-sphere.

The construction stretches a region into a very long round cylinder and closes it with smooth caps. It fixes the cylinder length at 10000 and rescales the resulting metric to the round sphere’s volume. The resulting weight stays smooth and strictly positive everywhere.

At a specified positive time, its scaled heat trace is greater than 13/20. The round sphere’s value is less than 321/500 at every positive time. Since 13/20 is larger than 321/500, the weighted example has a strictly larger time maximum. Both maxima occur at finite positive times.
result: Let g₀ be the unit round metric on S³, let Δg₀ be the positive Laplacian, and define Y₀ = Δg₀ + 3/4 and YW = W^(-1/2) Y₀ W^(-1/2) on L²(dVg₀). There is one specified smooth strictly positive weight W with ∫S³ W^(3/2) dVg₀ = 2π² and an explicitly defined t* > 0 such that (t*)^(3/2) Tr(exp(-t* YW)) > 1106714561/1700054750 > 13/20, while max over t > 0 of t^(3/2) Tr(exp(-t Y₀)) < 321/500.

For the paper’s capped cylinder gL = WL g₀ with L = 10000 and VL = vol(gL), set a = (2π²/VL)^(2/3), W = aWL and t* = 4a. The paper defines WL by an explicit flat smooth cutoff and a convergent volume integral. These expressions specify one finite weight and time.
Both the weighted and round scaled heat traces attain their maxima at positive finite times. The dimension-three example refutes the comparison quantified over all dimensions n ≥ 3.
why_it_works: Classical cylindrical conformal geometry supplies the long product region. The explicit caps extend smoothly over both poles, and the final constant rescaling gives the exact volume normalization. Conformal covariance identifies the geometric Yamabe operator with the stated symmetric weighted operator.

Dirichlet sine functions on the cylinder, extended by zero, belong to the global quadratic-form domain. The min–max principle bounds every eigenvalue needed for an infinite heat-trace lower sum. A Gaussian integral and the finite cap-volume estimate give the displayed weighted lower bound.

The round sphere has an explicit spectrum. Gaussian Poisson summation controls small times, analytic interval and infinite-tail estimates control the middle range, and monotonicity controls large times. Exact rational inequalities complete the bound for every positive time.

The common small-time limit and decay at infinity, together with continuity and values above the small-time limit, ensure that both maxima are attained. The finite arithmetic certificates support these analytic arguments.
limitations: The example is in dimension three. The comparison restricted to n ≥ 4 and the separate monotonicity conjecture for n ≥ 4 remain unaddressed.

The theorem uses the specified finite length, smooth caps, exact normalization and witness time. It makes no assertion that the witness time is a maximizing time, that a maximizing time is unique, or that the estimates are uniform over a degenerating family.

The cylindrical geometry, conformal covariance, Dirichlet trial spaces, min–max principle and Gaussian heat estimates are classical. The contribution presented here is a specified finite quantitative application to the historical comparison, with checkable bounds.

The historical source comparison is bounded. The inspected author versions and selected transformed-trace interfaces do not establish exhaustive coverage of the literature. Historical priority, worldwide firstness and continued worldwide openness remain unestablished.

The final 2011 Ammann–Jammes publisher chapter and complete final 2002 Morpurgo journal PDF were not authenticated in the underlying source comparison. The exact author editions and selected web interfaces used are distinguished in the accompanying materials.

metadata.title: A finite counterexample to the weighted Yamabe heat trace comparison
metadata.description:
We give a finite smooth counterexample in dimension three to Conjecture 1 in Carlo Morpurgo's contribution to Oberwolfach Report 6/2009, printed pages 421-422. On the round three-sphere the positive weighted Yamabe operator W^(-1/2)(Delta+3/4)W^(-1/2) is normalized by the conformal volume integral of W^(3/2) equal to 2 pi^2. An explicitly capped cylinder of length 10000 gives a specified weight and positive time with scaled heat trace greater than 13/20; the round maximum is less than 321/500. Both maxima are attained. This refutes the assertion over all dimensions n at least 3. The assertion restricted to n at least 4 and the adjacent monotonicity question remain unaddressed.

The qualitative negative answer is a straightforward assembled consequence of classical cylindrical conformal geometry, a chosen fixed rescaled cap, Dirichlet min-max and an elementary round trace bound. Ammann and Jammes and the earlier constructions cited there are credited; no new geometric or spectral mechanism is claimed. The note records an explicit finite quantitative application to the historical comparison and exact rational certificates. Related transformed-trace inequalities of Morpurgo are distinguished. A dated bounded priority audit found no earlier explicitly assembled exact refutation in its inspected corpus, with version and retrieval limits recorded. Historical priority of the exact application, worldwide firstness and current openness are unestablished.

The deposit contains a four-page research note and a verification archive with editable source, all 42 frozen original files and three evidence archives, fresh independent mathematical and bounded-priority reviews, exact arithmetic and integrity checks, and semantic negative controls. Downloaded primary publications are excluded; source locators and hashes are retained. OpenAI tools were used extensively in development, solving, drafting, coding and adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint; no completed external human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification is claimed. Arithmetic and integrity checks do not prove the analytic lemmas or certify priority.

Morpurgo, Cwikel-Lieb-Rozenblum bounds and heat kernel inequalities, item (16) in Problems from the Oberwolfach Workshop, Low Eigenvalues of Laplace and Schrodinger Operators, Oberwolfach Reports 6 (2009), 355-428, printed pp. 421-422, Conjecture 1. https://doi.org/10.4171/OWR/2009/06

B. Ammann and P. Jammes, The supremum of first eigenvalues of conformally covariant operators in a conformal class, Variational Problems in Differential Geometry, LMS Lecture Note Series 394 (2011), 1-23. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511863219.002. First preprint arXiv:0708.0529 (2007); inspected author manuscript dated December 8, 2008.
